content.what_it_is: MATLAB error-analysis script that loads numerical elevation columns for stations 2-12 and retains both vertically offset and unshifted forms (lines 5-12), constructs a 12-entry filename table for experimental records (lines 17-28), loads those records and retains columns 2-12 (lines 30-39), compares each of 11 data/model standard deviations (lines 41-47), and reports an RMSE normalized by the maximum data standard deviation (line 49).
entities: fdir path prefix assigned at line 3
k loop variable defined at lines 5, 30, 37, and 41
num formatted suffix assigned at lines 6 and 31
gage numerical station matrix assigned at line 7
z vertically shifted numerical matrix populated at line 8
model unshifted numerical matrix populated at line 9
time assigned from the final numerical gage at line 11
model_time copied from time at line 12
fnam filename character table populated at lines 17-28
gage_m experimental record assigned at line 32
en experimental-record matrix populated at line 33
data_time synthesized time coordinate assigned at line 36
data selected experimental matrix populated at line 38
data_eta current experimental series assigned at line 42
model_eta current numerical series assigned at line 43
error normalized aggregate RMSE assigned at line 49

equations.ref: vertical display offset for numerical stations
unshifted centimetre numerical series mapped from station k to model column k-1
experimental time coordinate with fixed 0.05 spacing

unresolved: relative_error is assigned without a k subscript at line 46 inside the 11-iteration loop on lines 41-47, so every iteration overwrites the preceding result and only the k=11 value survives; this is inconsistent with the indexed std_data and std_model outputs on lines 44-45.

Lines 7-12 overwrite gage for each numerical station and take time/model_time only from the final station. Those coordinates are never used when standard deviations are compared at lines 41-49, and the separately synthesized data_time at line 36 is also unused, so no sampling interval, duration, or time alignment check connects the two data sources.

Lines 44-46 divide by std_data(k) with no zero/non-finite guard, and line 49 divides by max(std_data) with no zero/non-finite guard; constant, empty, or invalid input can yield NaN or Inf and defeat the error metric.
The rmse call at line 49 relies on a function not defined in this file; compatibility depends on an external MATLAB/toolbox or path-provided implementation.

num is recomputed at line 31 but is not used by the experimental-file load at line 32, which instead indexes fnam; this is a copy/paste residue and can falsely suggest that the numeric suffix controls the file mapping.

The filename table is written by column at lines 17-28 and each column is passed directly to load at line 32. The file does not establish whether the target MATLAB/Octave load interface accepts a column character vector; environments requiring a row character vector will reject fnam(:,k).

Lines 7-9 require every numerical file to have a second column and equal row count, while lines 32-33 require each experimental load to be a single compatible-length vector. None of these file-shape interfaces is checked.
